401.08.question: As a Canadian VFR private pilot, what flight-condition details must your personal log record for each flight?
401.08.ground_truth: It must record the flight conditions with respect to day, night, VFR and IFR.

401.08.question: If you log a flight in an aeroplane, what route-related details must be entered besides the aircraft information and flight time?
401.08.ground_truth: For an aeroplane flight, the log must include the place of departure and the place of arrival, and all of the intermediate take-offs and landings.

401.08.question: Who is allowed to make an entry in a personal log?
401.08.ground_truth: Only the holder of the log, or someone authorized by the holder, may make an entry.

401.12.question: If a flight crew permit is issued as a booklet label, what three conditions must be met for it to be valid?
401.12.ground_truth: It is valid only if the label is affixed in an aviation document booklet, the booklet number on the label matches the booklet number, and the booklet is signed by the holder.
401.12.evidence_quote: (a) the label is affixed in an aviation document booklet;

401.12.question: When does the validity period start and end for a flight crew permit or licence issued as a booklet label?
401.12.ground_truth: It starts on the day it is issued and ends on the expiry date of the aviation document booklet in which it is affixed.
401.12.evidence_quote: starts on the day on which it is issued and ends on the expiry date of the aviation document booklet in which it is affixed.

401.12.question: A Canadian VFR private pilot has an aviation document booklet with a flight crew permit affixed in it, but no flight crew licence affixed in it. What is the booklet's expiry date?
401.12.ground_truth: The expiry date is the first day of the 121st month following the day on which the booklet was issued.
401.12.evidence_quote: the first day of the 121st month following the day on which the booklet was issued.

401.05.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot, what are the general recency options to exercise the privileges of a flight crew permit, licence, or rating (excluding a flight engineer licence)?
401.05.ground_truth: The pilot may do so only if, within the preceding five years, they acted as PIC or co-pilot, or completed an approved initial or recurrent pilot training program in a Level C or D full-flight simulator, or within the preceding 12 months completed a flight review, had the required logbook certification, and passed the appropriate examination.
401.05.evidence_quote: the holder has acted as pilot-in-command or co-pilot of an aircraft within the five years preceding the flight;

401.05.question: If a passenger is being carried, what recency must a pilot licence holder meet before exercising licence privileges in an aircraft?
401.05.ground_truth: The holder must have completed recurrent training within the 24 months preceding the flight, and must also have completed the required recent take-offs and landings within the six months preceding the flight for the aircraft type, category, and class or simulator conditions that apply.

401.05.evidence_quote: shall retain a record of having met the applicable recency requirements set out in subsection (3) or (3.1) for three years.

401.22.question: Under day VFR, what kind of aeroplane may the holder of a pilot permit — recreational — aeroplane act as pilot-in-command of, and what passenger limit applies?
401.22.ground_truth: The holder may act as pilot-in-command of an endorsed class and type of aeroplane if it is a single-engined, non-high-performance aeroplane designed or type-certificated for a maximum of four persons, and no more than one passenger is carried on board.

401.22.question: May the holder act as pilot-in-command or co-pilot for flight training or a flight test, and if so, what conditions apply?
401.22.ground_truth: Yes, but only for the sole purpose of the holder’s flight training or flight test. For flight training, it must be under the direction and supervision of a qualified flight instructor and no passenger may be carried. For a flight test, it must be conducted in accordance with section 401.15 and no passenger may be carried.

401.19.question: Under CAR 401.19, may a student pilot permit holder act as pilot-in-command on a daytime VFR training flight in Canada with no passengers on board?
401.19.ground_truth: Yes. A student pilot permit holder may act as pilot-in-command if the flight is for the holder’s flight training, conducted in Canada, under day VFR, under the required direction and supervision, and with no passenger carried on board.
401.19.evidence_quote: the flight is conducted for the purpose of the holder’s flight training;

401.19.question: If a student pilot permit holder is enrolled in an integrated course, can they act as pilot-in-command on a night VFR flight?
401.19.ground_truth: Yes. Despite the day-VFR limit in paragraph (1)(c), an enrolled integrated-course student pilot permit holder may act as pilot-in-command during a flight conducted under day or night VFR.
401.19.evidence_quote: the holder of a student pilot permit who is enrolled in an integrated course may act as pilot-in-command during a flight that is conducted under day or night VFR.

401.03.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot acting as a flight crew member, what items must be held, valid, and producible when exercising the privileges?
401.03.ground_truth: The person must hold the appropriate permit, licence or rating, it must be valid, the person must hold the appropriate medical certificate, and the person must be able to produce the permit, licence or rating and the certificate when exercising those privileges.
401.03.evidence_quote: (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), no person shall act as a flight crew member or exercise the privileges of a flight crew permit, licence or rating unless

401.03.question: Can a pilot use the privileges of a foreign licence validation certificate without signing it and carrying it?
401.03.ground_truth: No. To exercise the privileges of a foreign licence validation certificate, the person must hold the appropriate foreign licence validation certificate, have signed it, and be able to produce it when exercising those privileges.
401.03.evidence_quote: (1.1) No person shall exercise the privileges of a foreign licence validation certificate unless the person

401.03.question: May a holder of a foreign-issued flight crew permit, licence or rating act as flight crew solely for their flight test without carrying passengers?
401.03.ground_truth: Yes, but only if the test is conducted in accordance with section 401.15 and no passenger is carried on board the aircraft.
401.03.evidence_quote: (2) A person who holds a military flight crew permit, licence or rating or a flight crew permit, licence or rating issued by a contracting state other than Canada may act as a flight crew member or exercise the privileges of a flight crew permit, licence or rating for the sole purpose of the person’s flight test where

401.26.question: Under CAR 401.26, may a holder of a private pilot licence — aeroplane act as pilot-in-command of an ultra-light aeroplane?
401.26.ground_truth: Yes. The holder of a private pilot licence — aeroplane may act as pilot-in-command of an ultra-light aeroplane.
401.26.evidence_quote: (b) pilot-in-command of an ultra-light aeroplane; and

401.26.question: For the holder’s own flight training, when may the holder act as pilot-in-command or co-pilot of any aircraft?
401.26.ground_truth: Only for the sole purpose of the holder’s flight training, and only if it is conducted under the direction and supervision of a flight instructor qualified in accordance with section 425.21 of Standard 425 — Flight Training, and no passenger is carried on board.
401.26.evidence_quote: (c) pilot-in-command or co-pilot of any aircraft for the sole purpose of the holder’s flight training or flight test where

401.28.question: May a private pilot licence holder receive reimbursement for a flight’s costs when carrying passengers, and what limit applies to who provides that reimbursement and what it covers?
401.28.ground_truth: Yes, but only if the holder is the owner or operator of the aircraft, the flight is not for hire or reward, and any reimbursement is provided only by the passengers carried incidentally to the flight’s purpose and is only for sharing fuel, oil, and applicable fees.
401.28.evidence_quote: The holder of a private pilot licence may receive reimbursement for costs incurred in respect of a flight if the holder

401.28.question: Can a private pilot with a private aircraft be reimbursed by an employer for a flight done on the employer’s business, and how is the reimbursement limited?
401.28.ground_truth: Yes, if the pilot is employed full-time for purposes other than flying, the flight is on the employer’s business and incidental to the pilot’s duties, and for an owned aircraft the payment is based on distance or hours flown and does not exceed direct operating costs plus fees charged against the aircraft for the flight.
401.28.evidence_quote: The holder of a private pilot licence may receive reimbursement from the holder’s employer for costs incurred in respect of a flight if the holder

401.30.question: May a holder of a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane with a daylight-flying-only restriction exercise private pilot licence — aeroplane privileges by night?
401.30.ground_truth: No. A holder of a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane whose licence is endorsed with a daylight-flying-only restriction shall not exercise the private pilot licence — aeroplane privileges by night.
401.30.evidence_quote: No holder of a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane whose licence is endorsed with a daylight-flying-only restriction shall exercise the privileges set out in paragraphs (1)(a) and (c) by night.

401.30.question: Until when may a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane holder exercise private pilot licence — aeroplane privileges?
401.30.ground_truth: They may exercise private pilot licence — aeroplane privileges until the end of the medical validity period specified for the private pilot licence.
401.30.evidence_quote: exercise private pilot licence — aeroplane privileges until the end of the medical validity period specified for the private pilot licence.

401.32.question: May the holder of a multi-crew pilot licence — aeroplane act as co-pilot of a turbine-powered aeroplane operated at night under VFR?
401.32.ground_truth: Yes, but only if the aeroplane also meets all listed conditions: it is a transport category aircraft, has a minimum flight crew document specifying two pilots, is of a type endorsed on the holder’s licence, and is operated under subpart 4 of Part VI or Part VII.
401.32.evidence_quote: may act as co-pilot of a turbine-powered aeroplane that is operated day or night, under VFR, VFR OTT or IFR, if the aeroplane

401.32.question: Can the holder of a multi-crew pilot licence — aeroplane act as pilot-in-command of any aircraft for their own flight training?
401.32.ground_truth: Yes, but only for the purpose of the holder’s flight training and only if the flight training is conducted in accordance with section 401.19.
401.32.evidence_quote: may act as pilot-in-command of any aircraft for the purpose of the holder’s flight training if the flight training is conducted in accordance with section 401.19.

401.34.question: Under CAR 401.34, what aeroplane pilot licence privileges does the holder of an airline transport pilot licence — aeroplane have, subject to subsection (2)?
401.34.ground_truth: They may exercise the privileges of a private pilot licence — aeroplane and a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane, subject to subsection (2).
401.34.evidence_quote: the holder of an airline transport pilot licence — aeroplane may exercise the privileges of a private pilot licence — aeroplane and a commercial pilot licence — aeroplane.

401.34.question: When may the holder of an airline transport pilot licence — aeroplane endorsed with a Group 1 instrument rating act as pilot-in-command of the aeroplane under CAR 401.34(2)(a)?
401.34.ground_truth: Only while engaged in providing a commercial air service by means of an aeroplane of a class and type covered by the licence endorsement, and only if the minimum flight crew document for that aeroplane specifies a minimum flight crew of two pilots.

601.06.question: May a Canadian VFR private pilot fly a VFR aircraft in Class A airspace without a Minister-issued authorization?
601.06.ground_truth: No. A VFR aircraft may be operated in Class A airspace only in accordance with an authorization issued by the Minister.
601.06.evidence_quote: No person shall operate a VFR aircraft in Class A airspace unless the aircraft is operated in accordance with an authorization issued by the Minister.

601.06.question: When may the Minister issue an authorization for VFR flight in Class A airspace?
601.06.ground_truth: The Minister may issue it only when the operation is in the public interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.
601.06.evidence_quote: where the operation of the aircraft is in the public interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

601.03.question: Which classes of airspace are included in Canadian transponder airspace under CAR 601.03?
601.03.ground_truth: Transponder airspace includes all Class A, B and C airspace, and any Class D or E airspace that is specified as transponder airspace in the Designated Airspace Handbook.
601.03.evidence_quote: (a) all Class A, B and C airspace as specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook; and

601.03.question: Does every Class D or E airspace in Canada count as transponder airspace under CAR 601.03?
601.03.ground_truth: No. Only Class D or E airspace that is specifically designated as transponder airspace in the Designated Airspace Handbook counts.
601.03.evidence_quote: (b) any Class D or E airspace specified as transponder airspace in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

601.04.question: May a Canadian VFR private pilot operate an aircraft in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace without authorization?
601.04.ground_truth: No. A person may not operate an aircraft in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace unless authorized by the person specified for that purpose in the Designated Airspace Handbook.
601.04.evidence_quote: No person shall operate an aircraft in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace unless authorized to do so by the person specified for that purpose in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

601.04.question: Where are the procedures for operating in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace and Class F Special Use Advisory airspace specified?
601.04.ground_truth: They are specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook.
601.04.evidence_quote: The procedures for the operation of aircraft in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace and Class F Special Use Advisory airspace are those specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

601.07.question: Can I fly my VFR aircraft in Class B airspace without either an ATC clearance or a Minister’s authorization?
601.07.ground_truth: No. A person may not operate a VFR aircraft in Class B airspace unless it is operated in accordance with an air traffic control clearance or an authorization issued by the Minister.
601.07.evidence_quote: No person shall operate a VFR aircraft in Class B airspace unless the aircraft is operated in accordance with an air traffic control clearance or an authorization issued by the Minister.

601.07.question: If I am flying VFR in Class B airspace under ATC clearance and it becomes evident I cannot remain in VMC at the cleared altitude or route, what must I do in a control zone?
601.07.ground_truth: If the airspace is a control zone, the pilot-in-command shall request authorization to operate the aircraft in special VFR flight.
601.07.evidence_quote: where the airspace is a control zone, request authorization to operate the aircraft in special VFR flight;

601.09.question: As a VFR private pilot, what must you do before entering Class D airspace if you are operating normally with radio equipment?
601.09.ground_truth: You must establish two-way radio contact with the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.
601.09.evidence_quote: no person operating a VFR aircraft shall enter Class D airspace unless the person establishes two-way radio contact with the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.

601.09.question: If your VFR aircraft is not equipped for two-way communication, when may you enter Class D airspace and what must you obtain first?
601.09.ground_truth: You may enter during daylight in VMC, but only if the pilot-in-command receives authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.
601.09.evidence_quote: may, during daylight in VMC, enter Class D airspace if the pilot-in-command receives authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.

601.15.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot, what is the minimum altitude requirement when operating over a forest fire area or within five nautical miles of one?
601.15.ground_truth: The aircraft must not be operated at an altitude of less than 3,000 feet AGL.
601.15.evidence_quote: over a forest fire area, or over any area that is located within five nautical miles of a forest fire area, at an altitude of less than 3,000 feet AGL; or

601.15.question: May a pilot operate an aircraft in airspace that is described in a NOTAM issued under section 601.16?
601.15.ground_truth: No. Operating an aircraft in airspace described in a NOTAM issued pursuant to section 601.16 is prohibited.
601.15.evidence_quote: in any airspace that is described in a NOTAM issued pursuant to section 601.16.

601.08.question: Before a VFR aircraft enters Class C airspace, what must the pilot receive from the appropriate air traffic control unit?
601.08.ground_truth: The pilot must receive a clearance to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.
601.08.evidence_quote: no person operating a VFR aircraft shall enter Class C airspace unless the person receives a clearance to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.

601.08.question: When may the pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft without two-way radiocommunication equipment enter Class C airspace?
601.08.ground_truth: During daylight in VMC, the pilot-in-command may enter if they receive authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.
601.08.evidence_quote: may, during daylight in VMC, enter Class C airspace if the pilot-in-command receives authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic control unit before entering the airspace.

601.17.question: Under CAR 601.17, when does Section 601.15 not apply to a pilot operating an aircraft for fire control work?
601.17.ground_truth: Section 601.15 does not apply when the person is operating an aircraft at the request of, or with the authorization of, an appropriate fire control authority for the purpose of assisting that authority in its operations.
601.17.evidence_quote: persons who are operating an aircraft at the request of, or with the authorization of, an appropriate fire control authority for the purpose of assisting the fire control authority in the conduct of its operations;

601.17.question: If a person is operating under a Minister’s authorization, what must be on board and how must the aircraft be operated?
601.17.ground_truth: The authorization must be on board, and the aircraft must be operated in accordance with any conditions specified in the authorization.
601.17.evidence_quote: No person shall operate an aircraft under the authorization unless the authorization is on board and the aircraft is operated in accordance with any conditions specified in the authorization.

601.18.question: May the Minister make an order that completely prohibits aircraft from operating over a specified area?
601.18.ground_truth: Yes. The Minister may make orders prohibiting aircraft operation over areas specified by the Minister, including absolutely.
601.18.evidence_quote: The Minister may make orders prohibiting or restricting the operation of aircraft over such areas as are specified by the Minister, either absolutely or subject to such exceptions or conditions as may be specified by the Minister.

601.18.question: Can the Minister allow exceptions or conditions in an order restricting aircraft operations over a specified area?
601.18.ground_truth: Yes. The Minister may make the order subject to exceptions or conditions specified by the Minister.
601.18.evidence_quote: either absolutely or subject to such exceptions or conditions as may be specified by the Minister.

602.01.2.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot acting as pilot-in-command, who is responsible for the aircraft’s operation?
602.01.2.ground_truth: The pilot-in-command is responsible for the aircraft’s operation.
602.01.2.evidence_quote: The pilot-in-command of an aircraft is responsible for its operation.

602.01.2.question: Can a passenger or other person interfere with, or try to interfere with, the pilot-in-command’s responsibilities?
602.01.2.ground_truth: No. A person must not interfere with, or attempt to interfere with, the pilot-in-command’s responsibilities.
602.01.2.evidence_quote: A person must not interfere with, or attempt to interfere with, the carrying out of the pilot-in-command’s responsibilities.

602.01.1.question: As a Canadian VFR private pilot, may you operate an aircraft in a way that is reckless if no actual harm occurs but the flight is likely to endanger someone or something?
602.01.1.ground_truth: No. The provision prohibits operating an aircraft in a reckless or negligent manner if it endangers, or is likely to endanger, the life or property of any person.
602.01.1.evidence_quote: No person shall operate an aircraft in such a reckless or negligent manner as to endanger or be likely to endanger the life or property of any person.

602.01.1.question: What specific kind of risk to people or property does CAR 602.01.1 prohibit a pilot from creating while operating an aircraft?
602.01.1.ground_truth: It prohibits operating an aircraft in a reckless or negligent manner that endangers, or is likely to endanger, the life or property of any person.
602.01.1.evidence_quote: No person shall operate an aircraft in such a reckless or negligent manner as to endanger or be likely to endanger the life or property of any person.

602.03.question: As a Canadian VFR private pilot acting as a crew member, may you fly 10 hours after drinking an alcoholic beverage?
602.03.ground_truth: No. A crew member may not act within 12 hours after consuming an alcoholic beverage.
602.03.evidence_quote: No person shall act as a crew member of an aircraft

602.03.question: Can a crew member operate an aircraft while using a drug that impairs their faculties and endangers safety?
602.03.ground_truth: No. A crew member may not act while using any drug that impairs the person’s faculties to the extent that safety of the aircraft or persons on board is endangered.
602.03.evidence_quote: while using any drug that impairs the person’s faculties to the extent that the safety of the aircraft or of persons on board the aircraft is endangered in any way.

602.05.question: During flight time, who must a crew member obey if the pilot-in-command has authorized that person to act on the pilot-in-command’s behalf?
602.05.ground_truth: The crew member must comply with the instructions of that authorized person.
602.05.evidence_quote: Every crew member on board an aircraft shall, during flight time, comply with the instructions of the pilot-in-command or of any person whom the pilot-in-command has authorized to act on behalf of the pilot-in-command.

602.05.question: What kind of instructions must a passenger comply with when a crew member gives them on board the aircraft?
602.05.ground_truth: The passenger must comply with instructions from any crew member that respect the safety of the aircraft or the safety of persons on board.
602.05.evidence_quote: Every passenger on board an aircraft shall comply with instructions given by any crew member respecting the safety of the aircraft or of persons on board the aircraft.

602.04.question: May a passenger consume an intoxicating liquor on board if it was not served or provided by the aircraft operator?
602.04.ground_truth: No. A person may consume intoxicating liquor on board only if it has been served by the operator, or if no flight attendant is on board, provided by the operator.
602.04.evidence_quote: No person shall consume on board an aircraft an intoxicating liquor unless the intoxicating liquor

602.04.question: Can a pilot/operator allow a passenger whose faculties are impaired by alcohol to board the aircraft if there are reasonable grounds to believe the impairment may present a hazard?
602.04.ground_truth: No. The operator shall not allow boarding where there are reasonable grounds to believe the person’s faculties are impaired by alcohol or a drug to an extent that may present a hazard to the aircraft or persons on board.
602.04.evidence_quote: no operator of an aircraft shall allow a person to board the aircraft, where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person’s faculties are impaired by alcohol or a drug to an extent that may present a hazard to the aircraft or to persons on board the aircraft.

602.02.question: If you have reason to believe you are not likely to be fit for duty, may you act as a flight crew member on a Canadian VFR private flight?
602.02.ground_truth: No. A person shall not act as a flight crew member if the person has reason to believe they are not, or are not likely to be, fit for duty.
602.02.evidence_quote: a person shall not act as a flight crew member or carry out that duty, if the operator or the person has reason to believe that the person is not, or is not likely to be, fit for duty.

602.02.question: Can a private aircraft operator require you to carry out a preflight duty when the operator has reason to believe you are not fit for duty?
602.02.ground_truth: No. The operator shall not require any person to carry out a preflight duty if the operator has reason to believe the person is not, or is not likely to be, fit for duty.
602.02.evidence_quote: An operator of an aircraft shall not require any person to act as a flight crew member or to carry out a preflight duty

602.10.question: May you start an aircraft engine if no pilot is in the seat, but you have taken precautions to prevent the aircraft from moving?
602.10.ground_truth: Yes. An engine may be started if precautions have been taken to prevent the aircraft from moving.
602.10.evidence_quote: (b) precautions have been taken to prevent the aircraft from moving; or

602.10.question: If you leave an engine running with no persons on board, must the aircraft be left unattended?
602.10.ground_truth: No. If no persons are on board and the engine is left running, the aircraft must not be left unattended.
602.10.evidence_quote: (ii) the aircraft is not left unattended.

602.08.question: As a Canadian VFR private pilot acting as operator, may you allow a passenger to use a portable electronic device if that use could adversely affect the aircraft or its systems?
602.08.ground_truth: No. The operator must not permit PED use on board if its use could adversely affect the aircraft or the functioning of its systems or equipment.
602.08.evidence_quote: No operator of an aircraft shall permit the use of a PED on board an aircraft if the use of the PED could adversely affect the operation of the aircraft or the functioning of the aircraft’s systems or equipment.

602.08.question: Can a person use a portable electronic device on board an aircraft without first getting the operator’s permission?
602.08.ground_truth: No. A person may use a portable electronic device on board an aircraft only with the permission of the operator of the aircraft.
602.08.evidence_quote: No person shall use a portable electronic device on board an aircraft except with the permission of the operator of the aircraft.

602.07.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot, when must the aircraft be operated in accordance with the operating limitations set out in the aircraft flight manual under this provision?
602.07.ground_truth: When an aircraft flight manual is required by the applicable standards of airworthiness.
602.07.evidence_quote: set out in the aircraft flight manual, where an aircraft flight manual is required by the applicable standards of airworthiness;

602.07.question: Under this provision, can a pilot rely on operating limitations shown on markings or placards?
602.07.ground_truth: Yes, if they are markings or placards required pursuant to section 605.05.
602.07.evidence_quote: indicated by markings or placards required pursuant to section 605.05;

602.09.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot, may you allow an aircraft to be fuelled while a propulsion engine is running if passengers are on board?
602.09.ground_truth: No, unless the applicable requirements of subsection 604.84(1), 704.33(4), or 705.40(3) are complied with.
602.09.evidence_quote: No person operating an aircraft shall permit the fuelling of the aircraft while an engine used for the propulsion of the aircraft is running and passengers are on board the aircraft

602.09.question: Does CAR 602.09 prohibit fuelling while a propulsion engine is running when passengers are embarking or disembarking?
602.09.ground_truth: Yes, fuelling is prohibited in that situation unless the applicable subsection 604.84(1), 704.33(4), or 705.40(3) is complied with.
602.09.evidence_quote: or are embarking or disembarking, unless subsection 604.84(1), 704.33(4) or 705.40(3), as applicable, is complied with.

602.12.question: For a fixed-wing aircraft, when is it deemed to be operated over a built-up area or open-air assembly of persons under this provision?
602.12.ground_truth: It is deemed to be over such an area if the built-up area or assembly is within 2,000 feet horizontally of an aircraft other than a helicopter or balloon.
602.12.evidence_quote: (b) 2,000 feet from an aircraft other than a helicopter or balloon.

602.12.question: May a take-off, approach, or landing over a built-up area or open-air assembly of persons be conducted at a location that is not an airport, heliport, or military aerodrome if it would likely create a hazard to persons or property?
602.12.ground_truth: No. Except at an airport, heliport or military aerodrome, such a take-off, approach or landing over a built-up area or open-air assembly of persons must not be conducted in a manner likely to create a hazard to persons or property.
602.12.evidence_quote: Except at an airport, heliport or military aerodrome, no person shall conduct a take-off, approach or landing in an aircraft over a built-up area or over an open-air assembly of persons, in a manner that is likely to create a hazard to persons or property.

602.14.question: For a VFR private pilot flying an aeroplane over a built-up area, what is the minimum altitude requirement under this provision if none of the listed exceptions apply?
602.14.ground_truth: It must be high enough to allow an emergency landing without creating a hazard, and in any case not lower than 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle within 2,000 feet of the aeroplane.
602.14.evidence_quote: for aeroplanes, 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle located within a horizontal distance of 2,000 feet from the aeroplane,

602.14.question: When not over a built-up area or open-air assembly, how close may a pilot operate an aircraft to a person, vessel, vehicle, or structure under this provision?
602.14.ground_truth: The aircraft must not be operated at a distance less than 500 feet from any person, vessel, vehicle, or structure.
602.14.evidence_quote: at a distance less than 500 feet from any person, vessel, vehicle or structure.

602.13.question: For a powered aircraft, can a take-off, approach, or landing be conducted within a built-up area of a city or town at a place that is not an airport, heliport, or military aerodrome?

605.29.question: When may a flight control lock be used on an aircraft under CAR 605.29?

605.32.question: For a private VFR flight, when is each crew member required to wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen if the aircraft is operating above 10,000 feet ASL but not exceeding 13,000 feet ASL?
605.32.ground_truth: Each crew member must wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen for any part of the flight at those altitudes that is more than 30 minutes in duration.
605.32.evidence_quote: each crew member shall wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen for any part of the flight at those altitudes that is more than 30 minutes in duration.

605.32.ground_truth: Each person on board the aircraft must wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen for the duration of the flight at those altitudes.
605.32.evidence_quote: each person on board the aircraft shall wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen for the duration of the flight at those altitudes.

605.38.ground_truth: It must be equipped with one or more ELTs that transmit simultaneously on both 406 MHz and 121.5 MHz, and for all aircraft over land the minimum equipment is one ELT of type AD, AF or AP.

605.35.question: As a Canadian VFR private pilot, if you plan to operate a powered aircraft in transponder airspace, what equipment must the aircraft have?
605.35.ground_truth: It must be equipped with a transponder and automatic pressure-altitude reporting equipment, unless one of the listed exceptions applies.
605.35.evidence_quote: No person shall operate an aircraft, other than a balloon or glider, in transponder airspace, unless the aircraft is equipped with a transponder and automatic pressure-altitude reporting equipment.

605.35.question: If the aircraft does not have a serviceable transponder and automatic pressure-altitude reporting equipment, can you operate it under the minimum equipment list exception?
605.35.ground_truth: Yes, if a minimum equipment list has been approved by the Minister for the operator under subsection 605.07(3) and the aircraft is operated in accordance with that minimum equipment list.

605.40.ground_truth: Only for testing, in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, and for not more than five seconds during the first five minutes of any hour UTC, if the ELT transmits on 121.5 MHz or on both 406 MHz and 121.5 MHz.
605.40.evidence_quote: A person may activate an ELT, in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, for the purpose of testing the ELT for a duration of not more than five seconds during the first five minutes of any hour UTC

605.40.ground_truth: The pilot-in-command must ensure the nearest air traffic services unit or community aerodrome radio station is informed, and the ELT is deactivated, as soon as feasible.

605.84.question: If there is a conflict between a Minister-issued airworthiness directive and a foreign notice, which one applies?
605.84.evidence_quote: In the case of a conflict between an airworthiness directive issued by the Minister under section 521.427 and a foreign notice, the airworthiness directive prevails.

605.85.question: After maintenance, may a Canadian VFR private pilot take off in an aircraft without a maintenance release if the work was identified as elementary work in the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards?
605.85.ground_truth: Yes. No maintenance release is required for tasks identified as elementary work in the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.
605.85.evidence_quote: No maintenance release is required in respect of tasks identified as elementary work in the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

605.85.question: If a maintenance release is conditional on a satisfactory test flight, who may be carried on board during that test flight?
605.85.ground_truth: Only flight crew members and persons necessary for making observations essential to the test flight may be carried on board.
605.85.evidence_quote: the aircraft may be operated for the purpose of the test flight if no person is carried on board other than flight crew members and persons necessary for the purpose of making observations that are essential to the test flight.

605.86.question: For a Canadian VFR private pilot, when is a take-off prohibited under this provision?

605.39.question: If an aircraft required to be equipped with one or more ELTs is operated without a serviceable ELT, what must the operator do when the ELT is removed from the aircraft?
605.39.ground_truth: On removal of the ELT, the operator must send the ELT to a maintenance facility.

605.88.question: After an abnormal occurrence, may a Canadian VFR private pilot conduct the take-off before any inspection for damage has been completed?
605.88.ground_truth: No. A take-off is prohibited until the aircraft has been inspected for damage in accordance with Appendix G of the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.
605.88.evidence_quote: No person shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has been subjected to any abnormal occurrence unless the aircraft has been inspected for damage in accordance with Appendix G of the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

605.88.question: If the post-occurrence inspection does not involve disassembly, who may perform it?
605.88.ground_truth: It may be performed by the pilot-in-command, as long as the inspection referred to in subsection (1) does not involve disassembly.
605.88.evidence_quote: Where the inspection referred to in subsection (1) does not involve disassembly, it may be performed by the pilot-in-command.

605.92.ground_truth: The owner must keep a journey log, a separate technical record for the airframe, each installed engine and each variable-pitch propeller, and an empty weight and balance report, except where the fleet empty weight and balance program exception applies.

605.95.question: For a normal powered-aircraft flight, when must the journey log be on board before take-off?

605.95.question: May a take-off be conducted without carrying the journey log on board if the aircraft is not planned to land and shut down anywhere except the departure point?

605.93.question: If you make an entry in a technical record, what information and formatting must you include?

605.97.question: If a Canadian aircraft owner transfers title of an aircraft to another person, what must be delivered at the time of transfer?

602.97.question: May a VFR private pilot who does not have the radiocommunication equipment required by subsection (1) operate to or from an uncontrolled aerodrome within an MF area, and if so, what conditions must be met?

602.97.evidence_quote: when approaching for a landing, the aircraft enters the aerodrome traffic circuit from a position that will require it to complete two sides of a rectangular circuit before turning onto the final approach path.

602.89.question: For an over-water flight requiring life preservers, when must passengers be briefed on those items, and what must the briefing cover?
